postData.contentHtml:
A somber incident in Barnegat Bay, New Jersey, has led to a grandfather being charged in connection with the tragic deaths of his two young grandchildren. Stephen Schneider, 63, from Bayville, faces serious charges after allegedly operating his boat while impaired by alcohol, resulting in a fatal collision.

The heart-wrenching event unfolded on July 19th, when Schneider's 28-foot Tidewater Center Console boat reportedly struck Intracoastal Waterway Marker #39. The impact tragically ejected his grandchildren, Mya Bella Golabek, 9, and Sigmund "Siggy" Paul Golabek, 7, into the water. Despite immediate efforts to bring them to shore and transport them to a hospital, both children succumbed to their injuries. Schneider's wife, Laurie Schneider, 64, was also on board at the time of the crash.

Following an investigation, Stephen Schneider voluntarily surrendered on Friday and has been charged with two counts of reckless vessel homicide/death by vessel, a second-degree charge. He also faces charges of operating a vessel under the influence and reckless operation of a vessel.

The incident has resonated deeply, sparking discussions online. While social media sentiment shows a "mostly positive" leaning, likely reflecting widespread sympathy for the profound loss experienced by the family, there is also "some debate" regarding accountability and the critical importance of safe boating practices, especially concerning alcohol consumption. This tragic event serves as a stark reminder of the devastating consequences that can arise from impaired operation on our waterways.
postData.title: Grandfather Charged in Tragic Barnegat Bay Boat Crash That Killed Grandchildren
postData.summary: Stephen Schneider, 63, faces multiple charges, including reckless vessel homicide, after allegedly crashing his boat while impaired by alcohol, leading to the deaths of his two young grandchildren in Barnegat Bay.
